title: test:pr never re-imports the OpenAPI spec, so Akto scans a collection that has drifted from it — a declared operation is not a scanned one
description:
> **Origin.** Parked on [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) comment `718362a9` (2026-08-28T22:30:04Z) under "Related, found today and unfiled for the same reason" — `issueCreate` was refusing workspace-wide. Filed 2026-08-29. **No new measurement was taken for this ticket**; the numbers are the ones recorded on 2026-08-28 against PR [#762](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/762>).

## BLUF

**Declaring an operation in the OpenAPI spec does not put it in Akto's scan collection. **`test:pr` does **not** re-import the spec — only `test:pre-merge` runs `feed-har` — so the collection Akto scans drifts away from the spec silently, and a PR that adds operations gets an Akto result that never touched them.

This is the [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) premise reaching one step further than that ticket states it. KS-712 says: an operation absent from the spec is invisible to both tools. This says: an operation **present** in the spec can still be invisible to Akto.

## Measured

On PR #762, which declares four operations (`GET`/`PUT` on `/api/privacy/settings` and `/api/settings/notifications`):

| operation | occurrences in the Akto report |
| -- | -- |
| the two endpoints #762 declares | **0** |
| control endpoint A | 105 |
| control endpoint B | 7 |

The two controls are what make the zero readable: the report was produced, it was parsed, and it does contain occurrence counts — the declared endpoints simply are not in it. Without the controls, `0` and "the grep could not have matched" are the same reading.

## Why it is worth a ticket rather than a note

The failure is **silent and it points the wrong way**. An author who declares a new operation, runs `test:pr`, and sees no Akto finding on it will reasonably conclude the operation was scanned and is clean. Under the current wiring that conclusion is unsupported: the operation was never in the collection. Every "Akto clean" claim in a Test Evidence block on a spec-adding PR carries this caveat, whether or not the author knows it.

This sits directly against the merge flow adopted 2026-08-25, where the **Test Evidence block carries the testing claim**. A block that says "Akto FAIL 3, none on a touched route" is true and still misleading if the touched routes could not have been scanned.

## Not fixed, and why

Re-importing the spec into Akto **mutates harness state** — the collection is shared, and @PeterObeden has live work on it ([KS-717](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-717)). Doing it unilaterally mid-review would corrupt someone else's measurements to fix a reporting gap. It belongs with the harness owner, alongside [KS-716](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-716).

## Possible shapes (for whoever owns it — not a design commitment)

1. Have `test:pr` re-import when the spec's hash has changed since the last import — cheap, and the common case is no change.
2. Fail `test:pr` loudly when an operation touched by the diff is absent from the collection, rather than reporting a clean scan of it. This is the honesty-guard shape already used elsewhere in the harness.
3. Leave `test:pr` alone and have the Test Evidence template require the author to state Akto collection coverage explicitly, so the gap is visible rather than assumed away.

Option 2 is the one that fails closed, but it is the harness owner's call.

nodes.body:
@kamil.kreiser — could you take a look? This is your ticket and I have **not** touched it, but there is now a measured reason it matters more than when you filed it.

Re-verified today on `feature/ks-1286-…` (2026-09-28): the premise still holds exactly as you wrote it. `test:pr` is `vitest run tests/prScan.test.ts` and `test:pre-merge` / `test:security` are the same shape — **none of them import**. The import lives only in `bin/setup.ts`, run separately, so a re-import still depends on someone remembering.

**Why it now looks like the largest lever on scan coverage.** Full OWASP run on slot 2, 50,162 results:

| bucket | count | share |
|---|---|---|
| `byDesignFilter` (template did not match the endpoint) | 36,946 | **74%** |
| `rateLimited` (429, new under KS-709) | 8,730 | 17% |
| `clean` | 2,338 | 5% |
| `notApplicableStack` | 1,717 | 3% |
| `authzPrecondition` | 419 | 1% |

`byDesignFilter` is by far the biggest bucket, and Akto's `api_selection_filters` match on **parameters** — which is precisely what your measurement showed the import restores: `loadParamsOfEndpoint` saw `identityCommitment` only *after* a re-import, and collection `urlsCount` went **190 → 352**.

**I am being careful not to overclaim:** most of that 74% is legitimate (194 templates × 348 endpoints — most genuinely do not apply), and I have not measured how much a re-import would recover. It could be a few percent. But it is the only bucket big enough for the answer to matter, and nobody has measured it.

Your false-zero warning is carried forward and is the part I would most want preserved in any fix: `getCollectionEndpointCount` read **325 before and after** an import that actually took it to 361, so the result must be verified on a **fresh re-read**, never on the value the import call returns.

Not picking this up — it is assigned to you and I did not want to take it without asking. If you would rather I did the harness side, say so here.

## BLUF

**Measured today: after a spec re-import, Akto CAN see `identityCommitment` at parameter level.** This ticket's premise — that `test:pr` never re-imports, so a newly declared field is invisible to Akto — is confirmed by the fact that the re-import was what changed it.

## Evidence

Ran the OpenAPI import against the widened spec (Peter's requirement 3 on [#760](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/760)), on a tree rebased onto `436f37bed` so it carried KS-721's field.

Two Akto instruments queried for `POST /api/anchors`:

```
/api/loadParamsOfEndpoint   identityCommitment 1x    control 'metadata' 4x
/api/fetchAllParams         identityCommitment 0x    control 'metadata' 0x
```

One instrument sees it, the other sees neither it nor the control — so the positive comes from the endpoint that actually holds request-parameter data, not from a lucky substring match.

**Collection state, before → after the import:** `OpenAPI Secuura API` urlsCount **190 → 352**, api_info **325 → 361**. 27 collections before and after, none created, none lost.

## ⚠ A false zero that will bite the next person

**The endpoint count read 325 before the import and 325 after.** `getCollectionEndpointCount` called immediately after ingest returns a stale `api_info` list; a fresh capture moments later shows 361. That is the KS-700 shape — an operation that plainly worked, reporting a number that says it did nothing. Anyone automating a re-import check against that call will conclude the import is a no-op.

Worth folding into this ticket's fix: whatever makes `test:pr` re-import should verify the result on a **re-read**, not on the value the import call returns.

## What this does not settle

The re-import here was manual and one-off. This ticket is about `test:pr` doing it as a matter of course, and that is unchanged — the next `test:pr` run still will not re-import. So the KS-712 sweep benefit remains dependent on someone remembering to import by hand.

*Measured 2026-08-31 (session 93) on the local Akto stack, from the #760 review thread. Local containers only, not a shared instance. No code written for this ticket.*
